input.rationale: Supplements the identity finding's durable knowledge with the usage anchor just registered, keeping its statement unchanged: the Ok semantics it relies on is the one the crate's own example presents, not only the handle doc.

knowledge.statement: drain_notifiers resolves a pending append_notify by index coverage before it considers leadership: for a pending call with a recorded assignment `(idx, ballot)` the arm `Some((idx, _)) if idx <= decided` is matched before `Some((idx, ballot)) if ballot < cur_ballot`, so once the node's decided index reaches idx the call resolves Ok(idx) without establishing that the entry at idx is the entry the call submitted. The ballot-based Superseded arm therefore only fires while decided < idx; with a current ballot the call would otherwise have to time out. In the probed construction node 1's own entry was accepted at index 1 and never replicated, node 2 was elected with an empty log and decided index 1 with its own entry, and after node 1 re-synchronized (Promise + AcceptSync truncating its log to node 2's) node 1's call resolved Ok(1) while the entry at index 1 was node 2's, not node 1's.
knowledge.conditions: omnipaxos_runtime actor; the caller's entry was assigned an index but was not adopted by the following leader (e.g. it never reached a quorum), the node then re-synchronizes with that leader so its decided index covers the assigned index with a different entry, and the call's deadline has not yet passed.

knowledge.statement: Every state transition the actor observes is published with an awaited send on the bounded event channel: detect_and_emit_events runs `self.event_tx.send(...).await` for OmniPaxosEvent::LeaderElected, ::Decided and ::Reconfigured, and it is invoked (and awaited) from inside the tick arm of the single `run` select loop. When the event channel holds RuntimeConfig::event_capacity unread events and the receiver is still alive, the send is Pending, so the whole actor task - not just egress - stops: op.tick() (election, resend and batch-flush timers), incoming-message handling, command handling and push_to_all_subs all stop until either the application reads an event or drops its receiver (a dropped receiver makes the send fail, which the code ignores).
knowledge.conditions: omnipaxos_runtime actor built by spawn_actor with RuntimeConfig.event_capacity >= 1; the application called subscribe_events() and holds a receiver it does not drain, or drains slower than transitions occur; no other task drops that receiver.

knowledge.statement: The other two egress paths of the same actor are deliberately non-blocking: protocol/control-plane messages go through enqueue_outgoing -> drain_outgoing_buf, which uses try_send and keeps unsent messages buffered (trimming oldest past the cap), and decided-log subscribers are fed with try_send in push_to_sub/push_to_all_subs, deferring the push when a subscriber is full. Incoming delivery awaits on the caller side (OmniPaxosHandle::handle_incoming), not on the actor side. The event channel is therefore the only egress whose backpressure can park the actor loop.
knowledge.conditions: Same actor; RuntimeConfig::outgoing_capacity / decided_channel_capacity reached while the receiver stays alive.

knowledge.statement: In the accept phase the core has no self-initiated refresh of the leader's knowledge of a follower's acceptance: resend_messages_leader's Accept arm only re-Prepares peers that are not promised and resends a pending StopSign or its decide, resend_messages_follower's Accept arm is empty, and flush_batch_follower replies only when a batch flush itself advanced the accepted index. Measured consequence at two and three nodes: whenever the lost Accepted receipts are exactly those the write quorum still needs (one at two nodes, two at three), the entry stays undecided for at least 100 configured resend periods, the leader keeps its own acceptance plus nothing, and the only protocol traffic after the drop is heartbeats; a later unrelated proposal then decides the earlier entry within one step, and a new Prepare/Promise cycle would re-advertise the acceptance through handle_acceptsync's reply instead.
knowledge.conditions: Sequence Paxos driven only through tick() and message passing, 2 or 3 nodes, error-free memory storage, in-order delivery of everything except the deliberately dropped receipts, no further client proposal and no ballot change during the window (so the accept-sync re-advertisement path stays out).

history.statement: In the accept phase the core has no self-initiated refresh of the leader's knowledge of a follower's acceptance: resend_messages_leader's Accept arm only re-Prepares peers that are not promised and resends a pending StopSign (or its decide), and resend_messages_follower's Accept arm is empty, so a dropped Accepted reply is never retried by either role. Over 500 logical steps (100 configured resend periods) with nothing else proposed, the only traffic after the drop is BLE heartbeats, the leader remains the stable leader, the follower holds the entry as Undecided with accepted_idx 1, and both nodes stay at decided index 0. The acceptance is only re-advertised later, either by a new client proposal (which makes the follower advertise a larger accepted index and decides both entries) or by a new Prepare/Promise cycle, where handle_acceptsync pushes a fresh Accepted carrying the follower's current accepted index.
history.conditions: Two-node Sequence Paxos configuration (write quorum = the leader's own acceptance plus exactly one follower receipt) driven only through tick() and message passing; the follower's single Accepted reply is dropped while every other message is delivered in order; the storage is error-free; no further client proposal and no ballot change during the window.
history.correction: Conditions narrowed to two nodes before the three-node case existed; the measured scope is now two and three nodes with quorum-critical losses, and the mechanism statement is unchanged. The earlier revision and its two-node receipt remain available.

knowledge.statement: The actor layer owns the OmniPaxos instance (spawn_actor consumes it by value) and exposes no compaction path: no handle method and no Command variant reaches OmniPaxos::trim/snapshot and the actor never calls them, so a runtime-only user cannot discharge the duty the repository's compaction documentation states. On the failure side, a storage write error is fatal in the core (the write paths call expect(WRITE_ERROR_MSG), 'Error writing to storage.'), that panic happens inside the task spawn_actor launched with no join handle kept, and the layer's failure contract has no storage-error variant - the only value for an absent actor is AppendError::Shutdown / RuntimeProposeErr::Shutdown - so the death reaches callers as the same value as an orderly shutdown, with the core's message lost.
knowledge.conditions: omnipaxos_runtime actor layer over any core instance; for the failure side, a Storage implementation that returns an error from a write operation (the trait allows this and defines the operations as rolled back). Source-settled, not executed.

result.summary: Completed a small consistency step with the remaining budget rather than starting work I could not finish: the identity finding's durable knowledge entry now carries the same usage anchor as the account I corrected last turn — its sources gained the crate's own example (examples/kv_store_async/src/main.rs:133-150, where the call exists for 'a specific entry whose durability the caller must confirm synchronously' and the resolved index is printed as 'durably decided at log idx ... safe to announce') — while its statement, conditions and cited executions (receipt 743518e2, event 1) are unchanged, so no body was gratuitously rewritten. Nothing else moved. Final position as the budget closes: four findings stand with their receipts, knowledge and scoped limits — (1) the actor layer's event egress parks the loop and, once enough nodes park, the cluster stops deciding (receipts ff4511e8, 76557a28, bbff5b4c; capacities 8/64/1024; corrected per-destination transport; 21.69s retrospective bound; the superseded transport-jam run kept as an excluded cause); (2) the core has no timer-driven repair for a lost Accepted reply, measured at two and three nodes with quorum-critical losses and only heartbeats on the wire afterwards (receipts 092538c6, 9f3f25cc; one accounting question closed by explanation); (3) append_notify can resolve Ok for an index occupied by another entry, bounded by measurement to entries the following leader did not adopt, with the adopted case shown truthful (receipts 743518e2, 78c53df3); and (4) the actor layer owns the instance but offers no compaction path, with the panic-to-Shutdown attribution chain and the repository's compaction documentation as the norm (source-settled). The one declared unfinished measurement remains the failure side of that last finding — a Storage whose write returns Err driven through the actor — which needs a delegating Storage wrapper that did not fit the remaining per-turn budget.
